title: streaming: robust lifecycle controls for client cancel/disconnect/reconnect + OpenAI compat fixes
author: Asha Kumar
release_notes: Adds robust streaming lifecycle controls: client cancel, graceful disconnect handling, reconnect/resume handshake, server-side idle and hard timeouts, and fixes for OpenAI-style streaming and function-calling semantics. Feature gated and rolling canary.
description: Motivation: production streaming workloads frequently observe transient client disconnects (mobile flaps, proxy resets) and deliberate client cancels. Without a consistent lifecycle, partial outputs, duplicated function-call events, or leaked resources can occur. This PR implements a lifecycle control layer for streaming endpoints: deterministic handling of client cancel requests, graceful disconnect + reconnect/resume handshake, server idle/hard timeouts, and a set of compatibility fixes for OpenAI-style streaming and function-calling semantics. Summary of changes: 1) lifecycle manager tracks active streams and assigns opaque stream_ids; 2) client-initiated cancel is now a first-class control (X-Redwood-Stream-Cancel header or control frame) that marks a stream as cancelled but preserves a resume token for short-window reconnection; 3) disconnect handling introduces a grace window (configurable idle_stream_timeout, default 30s) during which the server keeps KV cache and partial function_call state; 4) reconnect/resume handshake: clients may supply X-Redwood-Resume-Token with last_event_id and desired offset; server validates and resumes without duplicating deltas; 5) server-enforced hard_timeout prevents unbounded resource hold (default 2m) and emits a final stream timeout event to clients and logs for observability; 6) OpenAI compatibility updates: ensure streaming events follow the delta/done model, preserve function_call.name on the initial function_call stream event and stream function_call.arguments as subsequent delta events to match downstream OpenAI consumers; 7) structured output enforcement: stream only emits a single well-formed JSON function call body when function calls are completed or on resumed sessions (prevents partial JSON emissions to logs); 8) feature-flagged rollout with 5% canary for 48h and metrics/alerts added to Console. The description below lists commits, changed areas, CI notes, reviewers feedback, and rollout plan.

review_thread: Diego: Can we guarantee no duplicate function_call.name emissions on resume? Asha: Yes — lifecycle stores the last emitted function_call meta and resume logic deduplicates by event_id. Lena: Make idle/hard timeout defaults configurable via cluster config (updated). Ethan: Please add observability metrics for resume success vs failure (added metrics and dashboards). Diego: CI flake on integration test; root cause was test race — added deterministic waits. Final: approved by Diego, Lena; Ethan approved after metrics added.
canary_rollout: enabled (5% traffic for 48h, metrics: resume_success_rate, resume_latency, cancelled_stream_leak)
observability_notes: Added structured events: redwood.streaming.stream_timeout, redwood.streaming.resume_attempt, redwood.streaming.resume_success, redwood.streaming.cancel_received. Console dashboard and alert created for resume_success_rate < 99%
backwards_compatibility: Maintains OpenAI streaming semantics; default behavior unchanged unless feature flag enabled. Clients that opt-in get resume semantics. No breaking changes to existing REST endpoints.
rollback_plan: Feature flag + runtime config. Immediate rollback by disabling feature flag and expiring in-flight resume tokens; quick path to purge lifecycle state if memory pressure observed.
notes_for_release: Enable feature flag for controlled rollout. Update SDKs: Python and TypeScript include helpers to surface resume tokens. See docs/api/streaming.md for example reconnect flows.
